findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month. Historical figures are archived for five years before being summarized and retired."

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews self-checkout usage at the end of each quarter. Branch-level totals roll up into the consortium's shared reporting dashboard."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph, or if self-checkout usage is actually relevant to the fines decision, state that connection explicitly.

findings.evidence: "compared with 86 percent at the branches that kept fines in place over the same period"
findings.fix: State the number and identity of the comparison branches so the comparison can be evaluated.
findings.location: "What the Pilot Showed" section, first paragraph
findings.violation: The document never states how many branches make up this comparison group, so readers cannot assess whether it is comparable in scale or composition to the 5 pilot branches.

findings.evidence: "dropped from 22 percent of respondents before the pilot to 5 percent after it... administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Reconcile the timing - clarify that the result reflects a 12-month snapshot, not the pilot's full duration, or explain why that is being presented as the pilot's outcome.
findings.location: "What the Pilot Showed" section, second paragraph
findings.violation: "After it" implies the survey was given at the end of the 18-month pilot, but the next sentence says it was actually given at the 12-month mark, six months before the pilot concluded - an internal inconsistency about when the "after" measurement was taken.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Present evidence that the non-pilot branches are similar enough to expect the same effect, or scope the rollout to account for that uncertainty (e.g., phased rollout with monitoring).
findings.violation: The pilot data covers only 5 of the 10 branches, yet the recommendation generalizes the result to all ten without evidence that the other five branches are comparable.

findings.evidence: "This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date... matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established."
findings.fix: Cite the specific pilot data defining "eventual return" as within 60 days, or remove the claim that this threshold matches the pilot's findings.
findings.violation: No 60-day window appears anywhere in the pilot description, which only reports an aggregate "on-time-or-eventual return rate," so the claim that this cutoff "matches" the pilot data is unsupported and appears fabricated.

findings.evidence: "The systems team plans to update the online catalog's fine-display field during the same rollout window."
